narrationTexts: I'll start by finding the remaining `db.query` call sites.
Let me get the complete list of remaining `db.query` sites (excluding `cache.query`, which is a different API).

No tests in the repo. `lib/db.js` still exposes `query` as `@deprecated`, and `execute` additionally accepts a `timeoutMs` option. The migration is mechanical and uniform, so I'll apply it across the 13 package files and verify.
finalText:
Migration finished. 36 call sites across 12 files converted from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `admin/variantAdmin.js`, `repo/supplier.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `admin/macroAdmin.js`, `repo/sla.js` |

Each file had the same three shapes (get-by-id, list, update); the SQL strings and parameter arrays are untouched, only the call form changed. The result matches the already-migrated files (e.g. `support/src/repo/macro.js`) exactly.

Verification: `node --check` passes on every `.js` file in the repo, and a smoke test through `packages/support/src/repo/sla.js` shows all four driver calls recorded as `form: "execute"` with identical SQL and params to before.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** — the last two `db.query` calls in the repo. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, "Do not edit — it is replaced wholesale on every upgrade, and local changes are silently lost." Patching it would be reverted by the next upgrade, so this needs either an upstream fix, a pin/patch file, or a shim. It still works today since `lib/db.js` keeps `query` as `@deprecated`, but it will break when the driver's next major drops it — worth tracking before that upgrade.
- **`cache.query(...)`** calls in the `repo/` files — that's `lib/cache.js`, a different API, not part of this migration.

One note: `db.execute` also accepts `timeoutMs`, which the old positional form couldn't carry. I didn't add it anywhere since no call site had a timeout need expressed; that's a follow-up if any of these queries want one.
